title: APPENDIX: CHRONOLOGICAL TIMELINE OF ARUNACHAL PRADESH

cells: Region part of ancient Kamarupa; various tribal kingdoms; Ita Fort built (est. 14th–15th c.)
Treaty of Yandabo — British take Assam; begin engagement with hill tribes
Inner Line Regulation promulgated; restricts entry to hill areas
Region declared North-East Frontier Tract under Governor-General
Simla Convention; McMahon Line established as boundary with Tibet
British administrative posts extended into tribal areas
WWII; Japanese threat to NE India highlights strategic importance
Sino-Indian War; China occupies NEFA; retreats after ceasefire
NEFA renamed Arunachal Pradesh; becomes Union Territory (20 Jan 1972)
First elected Legislative Assembly; P.K. Thungan becomes first CM
Full Statehood: Arunachal Pradesh becomes 24th state of India (20 Feb 1987)
Bugun Liocichla discovered at Eagle Nest WLS — one of most significant ornithological finds
CM Dorjee Khandu dies in helicopter crash; Jarbom Gamlin briefly takes over
First train reaches Naharlagun; Donyi-Polo Airport (Hollongi) foundation laid
Several new districts created (Lepa Rada, Siang, Lower Siang, etc.)
Vibrant Villages Programme launched for border villages
Sela Tunnel inaugurated (March 2024); Hollongi Airport (Donyi-Polo) becomes operational

blocks.content: On February 20, 1987, Arunachal Pradesh officially became the 24th State of the Indian Union.

rows: Renamed Arunachal Pradesh; UT status granted
Became 24th State of India via 53rd Amendment Act

items: The 53rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1986 conferred full statehood to Arunachal Pradesh.
NEFA was administered by the Governor of Assam acting as the agent of the President of India prior to 1972.
Arunachal Pradesh Day is celebrated annually on February 20 to mark its statehood.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: 1914: The McMahon Line was agreed upon at the Simla Convention as the boundary between Tibet and British India.
1954: The North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA) was formally constituted under the Ministry of External Affairs.
1972: NEFA was renamed 'Arunachal Pradesh' and elevated to Union Territory status on January 20, 1972.
1987: On February 20, 1987, Arunachal Pradesh achieved full statehood, becoming the 24th state of India.
